strings.name: Paul Kagame
strings.summary: Raised as a refugee in Uganda, Kagame led the Rwandan Patriotic Front from 1990, became Rwanda’s central leader after 1994 and president in 2000. Reconstruction, public services and the digital economy are priorities, while political repression and intervention in Congo draw international criticism. Rwanda denies supporting M23; US sanctions on its defence institutions in 2026 underscore continuing regional disputes.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; reviewed on 15 November. This is not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Has long led Rwanda, advancing postwar reconstruction and the digital economy while his governance model and regional-security policies are widely debated.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: Tambwe area in present-day southern Rwanda.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Schooling in Uganda, including refugee schools, followed by military training; attended training at Fort Leavenworth in 1990.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Postwar reconstruction
strings.highlights.h1.text: Long led the state, promoting infrastructure, public health and the digital economy.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Regional influence and controversy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Centralized governance, treatment of opponents and Congo security policy receive extensive debate and criticism.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Defence institutions faced US sanctions
strings.timeline.t1.text: The US sanctioned Rwanda’s defence ministry over alleged M23 support; Rwanda denies backing the group.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Reelected president
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won reelection in a contest with restricted space for opposition participation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Chaired African Union
strings.timeline.t3.text: Served as rotating AU chair, promoting institutional reforms.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Constitution changed term framework
strings.timeline.t4.text: A referendum approved constitutional changes allowing further presidential bids.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became president
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Pasteur Bizimungu following his resignation.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Became vice president and defence minister
strings.timeline.t6.text: Entered national leadership after RPF military victory ended the genocide.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Led Rwandan Patriotic Front
strings.timeline.t7.text: Took command after the previous leader was killed in battle.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Birth and displacement
strings.timeline.t8.text: Born in Rwanda and fled with his family to Uganda during childhood.
